results.fact: High camp: Camp Muir vs camps below it on the traverse
results.evidence: Bivy-only dispute. The single Camp Muir entry does not serve this route: approach, approach_variants, beta, pitch_detail and itinerary all leave the Muir track near 8,600 ft and camp on the Cowlitz/Ingraham glaciers or Cathedral Rocks cleaver. Left to the camping clean-up; no bivy patch written.

The row's argument against June rests on road.status/closures ('opens late June to early July'), but that describes the Sunrise Road: the park's opening schedule lists the White River Road to the campground lot (which passes the Fryingpan Creek trailhead) about a month earlier (e.g. May 25 vs June 22 for Sunrise), and the park's trailhead page says the road is open June-October. Late-May and June ascents of Little Tahoma are commonly reported. So June may well be a valid window and the Jul-Sep season plus the road text may be what is wrong; not settled by two agreeing sources on the climbing window, so no patch. The same road.status/closures wording appears on the East Shoulder row.

results.correct_value: NPS entrance fee (no NW Forest Pass); climbing registration + $82 fee required on glaciers/above 10,000 ft
results.evidence: The park's climbing page requires registration and an $82 per-person cost-recovery fee for anyone on a glacier or above ~10,000 ft; the park climbing-ranger permits page states the same fee and in-person registration. The route is inside Mount Rainier NP, where the park entrance fee applies, not a USFS Northwest Forest Pass.

patches.expect: Northwest Forest Pass required ($5/day or $30/annual). No specific climbing permit.
patches.value: Inside the national park, so a Northwest Forest Pass does not apply; the park entrance fee does. Climbing registration and the per-person climbing fee are required before going onto a glacier or above 10,000 ft.

results.correct_value: Pre-dawn alpine start (~2:00 AM) so the summit is reached around 8 AM and the block is left by mid-morning; leg durations unchanged
results.evidence: A guided itinerary for this route leaves Meany Crest early 'to get near the summit by sunrise', with 5-6 hours camp to summit; a club trip report on the East Shoulder records a 1:40 AM start. Both support the turnaround and the day note's own 'alpine start', not a 6:30 AM departure. The schedule was shifted earlier by 4.5 hours keeping every leg's duration.

results.fact: Summit finish class (Class 2-3 in itinerary vs Class 3-4 grade)
results.evidence: Same finding as on the East Shoulder row (same line): route sources describe the final summit scramble as short, exposed Class 3-4 (the final step Class 4); grade and rock_grade on this row agree. The itinerary's 'Class 2-3' finish understates it.

results.correct_value: No rappel required; most downclimb the summit block, an old anchor allows an optional short rappel
results.evidence: A SummitPost trip report notes an old rappel anchor on the summit scramble that proved useful for the descent, and club trip reports rig anchors/fixed lines on the summit block; a guided itinerary simply reverses the route to camp with no rappel. So a rappel is optional, not 'common' and not impossible.

patches.value: None required; most parties downclimb the summit block, though an old anchor on the final step allows an optional short rappel.

results.evidence: Route descriptions give the East Shoulder finish as Class 3-4 with a short, very exposed Class 4 final scramble (~30 ft); grade, rock_grade, pitch_detail and climbing_route agree. The itinerary's 'Class 2-3' is the outlier.

A Rainier visitor guide puts the Fryingpan Creek footbridge about 3 miles in at 5,250 ft; a waterfall survey gives 3.4 miles to the footbridge, beside falls at 5,181 ft. Both agree with approach_variants (3.2 mi, ~1,400 ft above a 3,800-3,900 ft trailhead); the waypoint's 2 mi / 4,300 ft is wrong. Pin coordinates left untouched (out of scope).

results.correct_value: Summer: no self-registration, register in person at a wilderness information center after paying online; self-registration only in winter
results.evidence: The park's climbing page says there is NO self-registration in summer (May 22-Sep 30) and self-registration at Paradise only in winter; the park climbing-ranger permits page says permits must be picked up in person at a ranger station. access.permit's 'self-issued for free' is wrong for this summer route. The Sept 15/16-30 overlap in access.notes mirrors the park's own published season dates, so it was left as is.
